channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Crusoé: Lula classifica como ‘pirataria’ pedágio de Trump em Ormuz
item.description: President Lula (PT) labeled Donald Trump's announcement of a 20% 'toll' on oil shipments transiting the Strait of Hormuz as 'piracy.' Lula compared the move to historical maritime extortion, arguing Trump is using the pretext of clearing the route to profit from international trade.

item.title: Moraes suspende visitas de Flávio a Jair Bolsonaro
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended visits by Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro, who is under house arrest, for violating a judicial order banning social media posts and misusing visitation rights to disseminate a letter supporting Flávio’s presidential pre-candidacy. The decision followed a similar incident in August 2025 and prompted backlash from opposition and allies, with the PT filing a request to revoke Bolsonaro’s house arrest.

item.title: Bolsonaro usa metáfora sobre ângulos para falar de “soma de forças”
item.description: Lawyer João Henrique N. de Freitas reported that Jair Bolsonaro used a metaphor of mathematical angles — complementary (90°), supplementary (180°), and explementary (360°) — to advocate for unity and 'summing forces,' referencing a handwritten letter supporting his son, Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, and emphasizing integrity and overcoming obstacles.

item.title: Moraes suspende visita de Flávio a Bolsonaro e dá 48h para explicar carta
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes suspended for 90 days the visits of Senator Flávio Bolsonaro to former President Jair Bolsonaro after the latter’s alleged letter supporting Flávio’s 2026 presidential bid was shared on social media. The defense has 48 hours to explain the letter’s origin and authenticity.

item.title: Movimento Imparáveis nega ter sido criado por Michelle: "Inspiração"
item.description: The 'Imparáveis' movement denied being created by Michelle Bolsonaro, stating she is only its main inspirational figure. The note clarified that the movement was planned by former PL Mulher team members but was never formalized as an institutional project. Michelle remains affiliated solely with the Mulheres Conservadoras movement since 2024.

item.title: Advogada compara trabalhador que perdeu a mão com Lula e é repreendida
item.description: A lawyer was reprimanded by a labor prosecutor for comparing a worker’s hand amputation in a workplace accident to Lula’s severed finger in 1964, stating that pain cannot be compared. The 1st Panel of the TRT-23 unanimously upheld the company’s obligation to compensate the worker, rejecting the claim of exclusive worker fault.

item.title: The Economist: Pix ameaça domínio dos EUA no setor de pagamentos
item.description: The Economist article argues that Brazil’s Pix instant payment system challenges U.S. dominance in global payments, reflecting a broader trend of financial sovereignty as nations develop their own systems to reduce reliance on American firms like Visa and Mastercard. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer criticized Pix as harmful to American companies and proposed a 25% tariff on Brazilian goods, but the Brazilian government, including Finance Minister Dario Durigan and President Lula, denies unfair competition, citing evidence provided to U.S. authorities. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro defended Pix against U.S. attacks but advised against linking it to international networks competing with American systems like Zelle.

item.title: Crusoé: Por que Lula caiu entre beneficiários do Bolsa Família
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll showed a 10-point drop in President Lula’s support among Bolsa Família beneficiaries, falling from 68% to 58% in first-round voting intention. This decline contrasts with rising support for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, though the exact increase is not specified in the text. The loss of confidence among social program beneficiaries may reflect dissatisfaction with economic management or perceived reduced effectiveness of the aid.

item.title: Governo registra baixo desempenho em metas da Saúde e do PAC, diz TCU
item.description: The TCU reported that the Lula administration underperformed in health and Novo PAC goals in 2025, achieving only 16.7% and 23.1% of targets, respectively, well below the overall average of 44.8%. Conversely, deforestation control and basic education exceeded the average at 53.5% and 58.3%. The court attributes the shortcomings to structural budget execution flaws and poor goal calibration, undermining public spending efficiency and strategic planning.

item.title: Lula diz que Brasil “não precisa morrer por conta do petróleo”
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva stated that Brazil does not need to rely on oil to survive and advocated for a transition to alternative fuels, emphasizing the need to 'fight' for the world to adopt a new energy model. He cited U.S. President Donald Trump as an example of someone who denies climate change and supported increasing the mandatory biodiesel blend in diesel from B15 to B17, a proposal submitted by biofuel sector entities.

item.title: Temporada de convenções: onde os presidenciáveis darão o pontapé inicial das campanhas
item.description: Presidential candidates for the 2026 elections have set the dates and locations for their official campaign launches during the party conventions period, running from July 20 to August 5. Most chose São Paulo as their launch site, including Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), Lula (PT), Renan Santos (Missão), and Ronaldo Caiado (PSD), while Romeu Zema (Novo) is the exception, launching in Brasília. After the conventions, parties have until August 15 to register candidacies with the Electoral Justice.

item.title: Ala do STF considera improvável revogação da prisão domiciliar de Bolsonaro
item.description: A faction within the Brazilian Supreme Court (STF) considers it unlikely that the reading of a letter by Jair Bolsonaro, delivered by his son Senator Flávio Bolsonaro during a live stream, would lead to the revocation of his house arrest. Court sources state there is no prohibition on writing letters, and the letter’s political-electoral content does not constitute improper use of social media by a third party, as Bolsonaro did not produce it for public dissemination. The controversy arises amid a public feud between Flávio and Michelle Bolsonaro, with federal deputy Lindbergh Farias (PT-RJ) arguing the reading violates the conditions of Bolsonaro’s house arrest.

item.title: Lula chama taxa dos EUA em Ormuz de pirataria
item.description: President Lula criticized Donald Trump's proposal to impose a 20% fee on cargo shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, calling it piracy and inconsistent with democratic principles. He noted that the U.S., which historically fought piracy, now seeks to profit from a conflict it provoked, which he described as abnormal and immoral. Lula emphasized that the strait was not closed before the conflict and that Trump's move represents a sharp reversal from his June 2026 stance, when he opposed toll charges in the area.

item.title: Lula enquadra cobrança de 20% de Trump sobre cargas em Ormuz como ‘pirataria’
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva labeled the U.S. proposal, led by Donald Trump, to charge 20% on cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz as "piracy," arguing that a nation historically opposed to piracy cannot now engage in it. Speaking at the Mauá Institute of Technology in São Paulo, Lula described the measure as maritime extortion. He also criticized Trump’s justification, which frames the fee as payment for ensuring regional security.

item.title: Lula diz que Trump faz 'pirataria' ao prometer desobstrução do Estreito de Ormuz, no Irã
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva condemned U.S. President Donald Trump’s proposal to control the Strait of Hormuz and charge 20% per oil tanker transiting the route, calling it 'piracy'. He linked the Middle East conflict to rising food prices in Brazil due to increased fuel transport costs, and reiterated that Iran does not possess nuclear weapons, labeling the U.S. justification a 'lie'. Lula also connected Brazil’s 12% export tax on oil to preventing foreign exploitation of the sector.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula visita o Instituto de Aeronáutica e Espaço
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva visits the Aeronautics and Space Institute in São José dos Campos to learn about the UGEE1000BR project, Brazil’s first nationally developed gas turbine powered entirely by ethanol for electricity generation. After the visit, he will make a press announcement at the DCTA campus, accompanied by Vice President Geraldo Alckmin and Minister of Mines and Energy Alexandre Silveira. The agenda underscores the government’s focus on technological innovation and sustainable development.

item.title: TCU aponta baixo desempenho do governo Lula em metas do PPA
item.description: A TCU reported that the Lula government's performance in meeting the PPA targets for 2025 fell below expectations, with Health and the New PAC showing the lowest results. The court noted that evaluated programs underperformed in key indicators. The assessment reflects challenges in implementing central public policies of the administration.

item.title: Lula alfineta delegação brasileira após eliminação na Copa: 'Que vergonha, ninguém voltou para o Brasil'
item.description: President Lula criticized the Brazilian national team after their 2026 World Cup elimination, noting that only one player, Danilo, returned to Brazil on the team flight while the rest remained abroad on vacation. He jokingly suggested that coach Carlo Ancelotti should hire a robot developed by a student, which he described as 'aggressive' and capable of securing a World Cup win. Lula made the remarks during a visit to the Mauá Institute of Technology in São Paulo, where he also praised the robot’s potential to improve the team’s performance.

item.title: Crusoé: Terceira via sobe de 11% para 27%
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll released on July 13 shows that 27% of Brazilians now prefer a 'third way' candidate — not supported by Lula or Jair Bolsonaro — up from 11% in March. This significant rise reflects growing dissatisfaction with the two dominant political forces and increased support for independent or centrist alternatives. The trend signals a desire for change and a break from current polarization.

item.title: Governo anuncia avanço para fase de testes na mistura do diesel
item.description: The government announced the start of testing phases to increase biodiesel blending in diesel from B15 to up to B25, with initial evaluations between B15 and B20 followed by tests up to B25. The National Biodiesel Testing Program, backed by R$30 million in investment and involving MME, MCTI, ANP, and research institutions, aims to ensure technical viability before any CNPE approval. Despite sector pressure to move directly to B17, government sources indicate a final decision may not occur until 2027.

item.title: Partidos nanicos falam em cansaço com Tarcísio e Haddad após somarem pontos em pesquisa
item.description: Third-place pre-candidates from minor parties in São Paulo say voters are tired of the policies of Governor Tarcísio de Freitas and former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad, opening space for alternative options in the polls. They argue that the weariness with these two main figures creates an opportunity for new voices in the state political debate.

item.title: Lula diz que Trump vai praticar 'pirataria' se EUA tomarem controle do Estreito de Ormuz e cobrarem 20% sobre cargas
item.description: President Lula accused Donald Trump of practicing 'piracy' if the U.S. takes control of the Strait of Hormuz and imposes a 20% fee on cargo transported by vessels passing through the area. He made the statement on Monday (13), calling such a move an abusive and illegal action under international law. Lula defended freedom of navigation and criticized potential unilateral actions by the United States.

item.title: Caiado afirma que ‘liderança não se herda’ após Flávio ler carta de Bolsonaro
item.description: Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized Jair Bolsonaro's (PL) letter supporting his son, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), stating that 'leadership is not inherited, it is demonstrated'. He argued that voters expect a president capable of making independent decisions during crises, without relying on constant approval from other leaders, citing potential tensions with Venezuela, Bolivia, and Argentina. The remarks came after Flávio read the letter live, in which Bolsonaro calls for unity behind his son's presidential bid and designates him as his spokesperson.

item.title: Eleitores avaliam vídeo de Michelle com críticas a Flávio Bolsonaro na nova pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows 35% of voters were unaware of Michelle Bolsonaro’s video criticizing Flávio Bolsonaro, while 40% believe the criticism will not impact his 2026 presidential candidacy. Lula leads with 47% voting intention against Flávio’s 44%, within the poll’s two-point margin of error, indicating a technical tie.

item.title: Nova pesquisa mostra Lula na frente, mas indica uma tendência preocupante para o petista
item.description: The latest BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula leading with 40% of voting intentions in the stimulated scenario for the 2026 presidential election’s first round, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro at 34%. However, the survey reveals a worrying trend for the petista: both leading candidates lost three percentage points compared to the previous poll, with voters shifting toward blank/null votes, undecideds, and other candidates — indicating a potential weakening of polarization.

item.title: Valdemar diz não ter dúvida de Michelle Bolsonaro na disputa ao Senado
item.description: PL president Valdemar Costa Neto said he has no doubt Michelle Bolsonaro will run for the Senate in the Federal District, despite her stepping down from PL Women leadership and controversy over a video criticizing her stepchildren. He stated the candidacy will happen 'if God wills it,' for the good of Brasília, the country, and the party. Michelle’s remarks have caused rifts in the PL, particularly hurting Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign, which already struggles with female voters.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula visita o Instituto Mauá de Tecnologia
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) visits the Mauá Institute of Technology in São Caetano do Sul (SP) to launch a series of commitments focused on research and technological development in the state of São Paulo. During the visit, he will tour divisions of engines and vehicles, laboratories in robotics, automotive and NSPi, as well as facilities for ethanol and biodiesel testing. The event includes a press announcement at 12h, followed by a visit to the Aeronautics and Space Institute in São José dos Campos, accompanied by Vice President Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) and Minister of Mines and Energy Alexandre Silveira.

item.title: Pesquisa BTG/Nexus mostra quantos são anti-Lula e anti-Bolsonaro
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows 25% of voters identify as convicted Bolsonarists, 24% as convicted Lulists, and 23% as non-polarized, with 7% simultaneously anti-Lula and anti-Bolsonaro. In a hypothetical 2026 Lula vs. Flávio Bolsonaro matchup, Lula leads with 47% voting intention against Flávio’s 44%, within the two-point margin of error. The survey, conducted among 2,003 voters from July 10–12, 2026, has a two-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: ‘Ele pode escrever, não pode falar’, diz Valdemar sobre pedido para Bolsonaro voltar à prisão
item.description: PL President of the PL party, impact of Jair Bolsonar letter, stating 'he can write, not speak'. The letter, disclosed by Flávio Bolsonaro, supports his son’s presidential bid and aims to unify the right, while Lindbergh Farias (PT) has asked the STF to revoke house arrest on communication restrictions on communication.

item.title: Cabo Gilberto reage a Caiado e pede que ele “pare de ajudar o PT”
item.description: Chamber opposition leader Cabo Gilberto Silva (PL-PB) criticized presidential pré-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) following remarks about Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ). In a social media post, Gilberto urged Caiado to stop 'helping the PT', escalating internal tensions within Brazil’s right-wing ahead of the 2026 elections. The exchange highlights divisions among Bolsonaro allies over electoral strategy and alliances.

item.title: Federação União-PP discute caminho da neutralidade e diálogo com PT
item.description: The União Brasil-PP Federation is considering adopting a neutral stance in the 2026 presidential election, freeing up state-level slates to avoid internal conflict. The move follows growing dissatisfaction with Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) campaign and Ciro Nogueira’s frustration over lack of Senate colleague support in the Banco Master case. To facilitate dialogue with the PT, Deputy Dr. Luizinho, PP leader in the Chamber, is being floated as a potential mediator due to his strong rapport with Lula’s party.

item.title: Orçamento gerido por políticos sem mandato desmoraliza ainda mais o Congresso
item.description: Federal investigations that former deputies without mandates, such as Eduardo Cunha and Valdemar Costa Neto, manipulated the public budget through secret parliamentary amendments, using party influence to direct funds toward personal power projects, in violation of constitutional mandate. Supreme Court Justice Flávio Dino ordered the freezing of BRL 6.1 million from Cunha and over BRL 100 million from Valdemar, proving a clandestine corruption scheme in Congress that subverts the popular will and undermines democracy.

item.title: JOTA Principal: Emendas de liderança destinaram R$ 1,3 bi em ‘novo orçamento secreto’ em 2025, diz relatório
item.description: In 2025, parliamentary leaders allocated R$1.3 billion in amendments without disclosing the true author, forming a new 'secret budget,' according to a Transparência Brasil report. The scheme, led by seven party blocs including the PL, directed R$818 million through the Health Committee and includes allocations made by Valdemar Costa Neto, PL president, despite not being a deputy. Minister Flávio Dino's asset blockade against him intensifies crises in Flávio Bolsonaro's pre-campaign.

item.title: O que está por trás do avanço das ideias de direita no Brasil
item.description: Brazil is experiencing a significant advance of right-wing ideas, with 44% of the population identifying as right or center-right in 2026, up from 34% in 2022. This growth is concentrated in behavioral issues such as guns, homosexuality, and religion, where the right now has 52% support. The rise in attributing poverty to 'laziness' (from 22% to 40%) and the preference for lower taxes and private services (50%) reflect an ideological shift tied to the growth of evangelicalism and Protestant narratives aligned with economic liberalism.

item.title: Eleições 2026: 50% rejeitam votar em Flávio; 46%, em Lula, diz pesquisa Nexus/BTG | LIVE CNN
item.description: Nexus/BTG poll shows 50% of voters reject voting for Flávio Bolsonaro, while 46% reject voting for Lula in the 2026 elections. The results indicate high rejection levels for both candidates, reflecting electoral polarization. The content includes video and sharing elements, but the focus is on the poll data.

item.title: Câmara indicou R$ 1,3 bilhão em emendas de comissão sem identificar autor, diz Transparência Brasil
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies recorded R$1.3 billion in committee amendments in 2025 without identifying the individual parliamentarians responsible, according to a study by Transparency Brasil. The amount represents 16% of the commission’s allocations and replicates the logic of the extinguished 'secret budget', with party leaderships listed as authors, though not necessarily the decision-makers.

item.title: Crusoé: Não tem cartinha que resolva
item.description: Jair Bolsonaro's second letter supporting his son Flávio's pre-candidacy does not change the 2026 presidential race dynamics, as it was already clear from the first letter released in December that he had chosen Flávio over São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. The move has no new electoral impact, since the preference was already known and consolidated among voters.

item.title: Lula volta a ter mais imagem positiva que negativa e avança em ranking liderado por Bukele
item.description: Lula rose to 5th place in the Latin American leaders' popularity ranking, with 50.6% positive and 47.1% negative image, reversing his previous negative net rating. The three-point increase in positive perception and one-point decrease in negative perception signal a recovery in his public image. The CB Global Data survey, conducted between July 3 and 8, 2026 with 6,271 respondents, shows Bukele leading with 67.4% approval.

item.title: Lula e o desafio do voo de galinha
item.description: The article discusses the political challenge faced by President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, comparing his current situation to a 'chicken flight' — a metaphor for an unstable and risky position where he must balance internal pressures from the governing coalition and social expectations without losing control. The analysis suggests Lula needs political skill to avoid sudden downturns while maintaining governability and advancing his agenda.

item.title: As duas próximas pesquisas da semana sobre a disputa pela Presidência
item.description: Two polls are expected to be released this week regarding the 2026 presidential race. Quaest will publish its survey on Wednesday the 15th with 2,004 interviews, and PoderData on Thursday the 16th with 2,400 interviews. The Nexus poll released on Monday the 12th shows Lula at 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 44% in a hypothetical runoff, a technical tie within the two-point margin of error.

item.title: Em culto na Itália, Zambelli se emociona ao orar por Bolsonaro e agradece Flávio: 'Não se envergonhou de me defender'
item.description: Former federal deputy Carla Zambelli, currently in Italy, participated in an evangelical cult organized by the group 'Patriotas em Roma', where she prayed for Jair Bolsonaro and those convicted of the January 8 acts, and thanked senators such as Flávio Bolsonaro, Eduardo Girão, Magno Malta, and Damares Alves for their support. She emphasized that Flávio never shied away from defending her during her imprisonment and stated that Brazil depends on his path, despite setbacks in his presidential pre-candidacy due to the 'Dark Horse' case and public disagreements with Michelle Bolsonaro.

item.title: Lula é o 5º presidente mais popular da América Latina em junho; veja a lista
item.description: President Lula (PT) rose from sixth to fifth place in the Latin American presidential popularity ranking in July, achieving 50.6% positive image according to CB Global Data. The ranking remains led by El Salvador's President Nayib Bukele of the far-right, with 67.4% approval. The survey, conducted online from July 3–8 across 17 Latin American countries, shows Lula's popularity improved from 47.6% in June.

item.title: Lula tem 47% e Flávio Bolsonaro, 44%, no 2º turno, mostra pesquisa BTG/Nexus
item.description: The BTG/Nexus poll shows Lula at 47% and Flávio Bolsonaro at 44% in a hypothetical runoff, technically tied within the 2-point margin of error. In the first round, Lula leads with 40% to Flávio’s 34%, narrowing his lead from 8 to 6 percentage points since the last survey. The study also reveals that 75% of Lula’s supporters back him as the best candidate to govern, while 62% of Flávio’s supporters see him as the most prepared candidate.

item.title: Greve dos caminhoneiros: o que se sabe até agora sobre a paralisação
item.description: Wallace Landim (Chorão), president of Abrava, called a national truckers' strike starting July 13 to pressure the Senate to vote on the Freight Floor Provisional Measure before it expires on July 16. The MP aims to strengthen enforcement of the minimum freight floor and penalize companies paying below ANTT-defined rates, which the sector views as essential for ensuring profitability, especially for independent drivers and small carriers. No official adhesion estimates exist yet, and the movement awaits a Senate signal by Tuesday, with potential expansion if voting stalls.

item.title: Governo aciona AGU após ameaça de paralisação dos caminhoneiros
item.description: The Lula government activated the Attorney General's Office and informed ministers of Institutional Relations and the Casa Civil to prevent a threatened truckers' strike set for midnight Monday (July 13), amid a Senate impasse over MP nº 1.343 (Freight MP). The measure establishes a R$ 5,000 national minimum wage for formal cargo transport workers and strengthens freight oversight, having been approved in the Chamber with a 'jabuti' pardoning fines for roadblocks after Lula's 2022 victory. Despite the strike threat announced by Abrava's Wallace Landim (Chorão), the government believes an agreement can be reached by Monday to enable the vote.

item.title: Os índices de aprovação de Lula, segundo nova pesquisa Nexus
item.description: A Nexus poll released on July 13, 2026 shows 47% of voters approve and 47% disapprove of Lula’s government, maintaining the technical tie from the June 29 round within the two-point margin of error. While 35% rate the government as good or excellent (down from 38%), 41% call it poor or terrible (down from 42%), indicating a slight qualitative deterioration despite stable overall approval. The BTG Pactual-commissioned survey interviewed 2,003 people by phone from July 10–12, with TSE registration BR-07981/2026.

item.title: Eleitores das capitais e regiões metropolitanas consideram Lula mais capaz de melhorar a vida dos brasileiros
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are technically tied in voter perception of who can better improve Brazilians' lives, with 45% and 42% respectively, according to a BTG/Nexus poll. However, Lula holds an up to eight-point advantage among residents of state capitals and metropolitan regions.

item.title: Pré-candidatos a presidente avaliam estratégias para os debates
item.description: Presidential candidates are shaping their debate strategies ahead of the 2026 election, with Lula (PT) as the primary target due to his polling lead and unique center-left position. The PT camp favors participating only in debates with strict rules, such as those on TV Bandeirantes and Globo, while Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) threatens to boycott debates without Lula. Candidates like Caiado (PSD), Zema (Novo), and Renan Santos (Missão) aim to gain visibility by positioning themselves as anti-Lula or anti-system.

item.title: Greve dos caminhoneiros: líder convoca manifestação para esta segunda-feira
item.description: Wallace Landin (Chorão), president of the Brazilian Association of Automotive Vehicle Drivers (Abrava), called for a truckers' strike starting at midnight on Monday (13) to protest the Senate's failure to vote on the Freight Floor Measure (MP 1.343/2026). He blames Senator Davi Alcolumbre for blocking the proposal due to political tensions following the dispute over Jorge Messias' STF nomination. The MP expires on July 16 if not approved, and the strike could worsen if no voting signal is given by Tuesday.

item.title: Equipe de Lula conta com neutralidade dos partidos do Centrão e defende acenos do presidente a eleitores de centro
item.description: Lula’s team expects Centrão parties (PP, União Brasil, Republicanos and MDB) to remain neutral in the 2026 presidential election, allowing local allies freedom, while the PSD may support Lula in states like Bahia. The strategy now is to capitalize on Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL) campaign crisis — including family rifts and judicial restrictions on Bolsonaro — to move beyond polarization and appeal to centrist voters.
